newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU starts probe of C. Lyonnais buy back of SDBO.
newsitem.headline: EU starts probe of C. Lyonnais buy back of SDBO.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had asked the French authorities to provide details on the repurchase by Credit Lyonnais of Societe de Banque Occidentale (SDBO) saying that the operation could have involved state aid.

The Commission particularly queried the absence of a tender for the acquisition of SDBO, stressing that the French government had only sounded out seven potential buyers, all of which were French and within a very limited period.

Credit Lyonnais paid 50 million francs ($9.7 million) for SDBO, which had earlier been hived off into a state owned vehicle designed to rid the bank of its loss-making assets in accordance with a restructuring plan for Lyonnais approved by the Commission in 1995.

The Commission said that an independent estimate had valued SDBO at 173 million francs. This was after the state-owned vehicle increased SDBO's capital by 274.5 million francs -- a detail which had not been given to other potential buyers.
The Commission gave France a month to reply.
Under the 1995 plan Lyonnais can only repurchase the assets divested into the special vehicle at the price they were then estimated to be worth or at their market value if higher.
